definitions.explanation: A member of the police force.

examples.japanese: {警官|けいかん}に{道|みち}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I asked a police officer for directions.

examples.japanese: {警官|けいかん}が{交番|こうばん}にいる。
examples.english: There is a police officer at the police box.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{警官|けいかん}になりたい。
examples.english: He wants to become a police officer.

examples.japanese: {警官|けいかん}が{交差点|こうさてん}で{交通|こうつう}{整理|せいり}をしている。
examples.english: A police officer is directing traffic at the intersection.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}があったので、{警官|けいかん}が{来|き}て{調|しら}べた。
examples.english: There was an accident, so a police officer came and investigated.

notes:
{警官|けいかん} is a neutral-to-formal term for police officer, commonly used in news reports and everyday adult conversation.

REGISTER DIFFERENCES:
- おまわりさん: friendly, used by children and in casual speech
- {警官|けいかん}: neutral, used in everyday adult speech and news
- {警察官|けいさつかん}: official/formal title, used in legal and administrative contexts

RELATED TERMS:
- {警察|けいさつ}: the police (organization)
- {刑事|けいじ}: detective

PLACES:
- {交番|こうばん}: police box (small neighborhood station)
- {警察署|けいさつしょ}: police station (full-size)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {警官|けいかん}に{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}される: to be questioned by police
- {警官|けいかん}を{呼|よ}ぶ: to call the police
